Time-Integrated SHAP Values for a Set of Observations

Source: R/plot_shap_beeswarm.R
compute_shap_matrix.Rd

Computes compute_shap for every row of newdata and, instead of averaging across observations (as the internal compute_shap_mean() helper does), keeps one time-integrated SHAP value per (observation, feature) pair together with each observation's raw feature value – the input needed for plot_shap_beeswarm.

Usage

compute_shap_matrix(
  model,
  newdata,
  baseline_data,
  times,
  sample.size = 100,
  features = NULL
)

Arguments

model

An mlsurv_model object from a fit_*() learner.

newdata

A data.frame of observations to explain (one row per observation).

baseline_data

A data.frame to sample background values from (typically the training data used to fit model).

times

Numeric vector of evaluation times passed to compute_shap.

sample.size

Integer, number of random feature orderings sampled per observation and time point (passed to compute_shap). Default 100.

features

Optional character vector of covariate names to explain, passed through to compute_shap. If NULL (default), inferred as setdiff(colnames(newdata), c(model$time, model$status)).

Value

A long data.frame with columns observation, feature, phi (time-integrated SHAP value), and raw_value (the observation's value for that feature).

Details

For each observation \(x\), per-time Shapley values \(\varphi_j(x, t)\) (from compute_shap) are time-integrated via the trapezoidal rule over the requested time grid, $$ \Phi_j(x) = \int_0^{T} \varphi_j(x, t)\, dt \approx \sum_{k=2}^{m} \frac{\varphi_j(x, t_k) + \varphi_j(x, t_{k-1})}{2} (t_k - t_{k-1}), $$ using the same integration already implemented by compute_shap(..., aggregate = TRUE, method = "integral"). This produces one summary contribution per (observation, feature) that reflects impact over the entire prediction horizon in a single value, which is what plot_shap_beeswarm visualizes – as opposed to a per-timepoint SurvSHAP(t) panel.

See also

compute_shap(), plot_shap_beeswarm()

Examples

# \donttest{
mod <- fit_coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno + diagtime, data = veteran)
sm <- compute_shap_matrix(mod, newdata = veteran[1:15, ],
                          baseline_data = veteran, times = c(50, 100, 200),
                          sample.size = 5)
head(sm)
#>   observation  feature         phi raw_value
#> 1           1      trt  0.00000000         1
#> 2           1 celltype  0.00000000         1
#> 3           1    karno  1.42998911        60
#> 4           1 diagtime -0.00466043         7
#> 5           1      age  0.02071794        69
#> 6           1    prior  0.00000000         0
# }
